thread:
maria: Starting a staged rollout of the new global rate policy (rate-limit-v2) now. Canary = 5% traffic, duration 30m. I pushed the config to staging earlier. Will monitor 429s/errors. ping if you see anything weird.

ashley: copying — what's the exact canary target? org-level or per-route?

maria: per-route on production routes matching /v1/generate and /v1/chat only. not touching embeddings for this canary.

simon: noted. any changes to the response headers for clients? x-rw-rate-limit still present?

maria: yes header unchanged. we added a new header X-RW-Rate-Policy: rate-limit-v2. payloads unaffected.

luis: putting a quick watch on payment and billing services — last time quota flip hit billing callbacks.

deploy-bot: :information_source: rollout started (rate-limit-v2) — canary 5% — 2026-03-15T15:00:21Z

support-bot: :rotating_light: alert — elevated 429s for /v1/generate from a subset of client-ids (svc-*) — rate=~12/min -> baseline 1/min

devin: can you paste a sample client-id that hit it? we need to see token behavior.

luis: client-id svc-checkout-9 reported repeated 429 with body: `{"error":"quota_exceeded","code":429}`. logs show rapid retries from payment-worker pool.

ashley: that error string looks like "quota_exceeded" vs older "rate_limited" we used. did the error schema change?

simon: no schema change. rate-limit-v2 introduced a short burst window and a per-second bucket. If a client does many parallel requests we may surface quota_exceeded rather than a soft 429 throttle.

maria: reproduction steps from support: curl example below (masked api-key):

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx" \
  -H "X-Client-Id: svc-checkout-9" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' &
# run 50 parallel
```

luis: I spun that locally against canary and saw similar. stack trace from gateway:

```
2026-03-15T15:07:12Z gateway ERROR client=svc-checkout-9 quota: token-bucket exhausted (burst=20/20)
2026-03-15T15:07:12Z router WARN route=/v1/generate upstream=runtime-12 429
```

devin: are retries exponential backoff? looks like payment-worker does immediate retries up to 3x.

ashley: which makes sense. immediate retries blow through the short burst. maybe our canary bucket params are too strict for certain high-parallel clients.

maria: current canary config snippet:

```
policy: rate-limit-v2
targets:
  - route: "/v1/generate"
    percent: 5
    burst: 20
    sustained_rps: 5
```

simon: suggestion: increase burst to 60 for canary or add a per-client burst delta for known internal svc- clients. We should avoid changing production buckets for external customers without careful look.

luis: +1 to per-client exception. We have about 6 internal svc-* clients that legitimately open many concurrent short requests.

support-bot: customer thread: #12345 — multiple "quota_exceeded" reports from checkout flow. Customers seeing failed payments. escalation opened.

maria: decision point: do we pause the canary and revert to rate-limit-v1 for 5% traffic, or patch params live?

devin: patching params live is quicker, but risk of config drift. pausing ensures no more breakage for external.

ashley: ops: can you increase burst only for svc-* client-ids and try to continue canary? quick ACL-like exception would be minimal blast radius.

luis: I can push an allowlist override for svc-* in 2 minutes. command below:

```
rdm policy set-override --policy rate-limit-v2 --match-client "svc-*" --burst 60
```

deploy-bot: :information_source: override applied (rate-limit-v2) for match-client svc-* — 2026-03-15T15:12:38Z

support-bot: support → customer 12345: asked them to retry after 60s. monitoring.

simon: metrics: 429s dropped 70% for svc-checkout-9 after override. other external clients show no change.

devin: can we still finish canary or extend to 10% after 30m? need to validate new burst semantics across more clients.

maria: propose: continue canary for another 20m but limit expansion until we run a short runbook to identify internal svc clients and either whitelist or adapt burst by client class. If new errors spike, rollback immediately.

ashley: +1. also can we document the error mapping so support knows which 429 => quota_exceeded vs rate_limited? That would cut down churn.

maria: noted. I'll add a short KB update.

support-bot: customer 12345 updated — payments succeeded after retry. marking incident monitor for 2h.

luis: follow-up: billing flow had slow queueing which amplified retries. we need to add jittered retry guidance in SDKs.

devin: creating a post-canary action list: 1) identify internal svc-* clients, 2) add allowlist or adjust burst defaults, 3) update support KB + SDK retry policy, 4) run broader canary with embed routes excluded, 5) schedule rollback test.

maria: thanks team. I'll leave the canary running under watch and call rollback if any externally-owned client starts to error. posting final note in 20m.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: canary still active — 2026-03-15T15:29:21Z

maria: 15:48 UTC — canary reached 25m. external client 47 not impacted. internal svc clients stable. extending monitoring to 2h and logging this as a near-miss. follow-up ticket: PLAT-8937 for whitelists + KB.

ashley: good capture. closing loop with support to confirm no more broken payments.

support-bot: confirmed, all affected customers cleared. closing escalation for now.

maria: ending thread — we kept deployment but amended policy with client overrides. postmortem-ish doc to follow. Thanks all.
